issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant duplicated rather than reasoned about.
issues.detail: The constant was previously imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat; now a second copy is declared in Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat with no comment binding the two values. Two independent sources of the same magic number is exactly the smuggled coupling that defeats local reasoning. State the invariant: which authoritative definition governs on-disk layout, and prove the duplicate cannot drift.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException -- a smuggled goto past the type system.
issues.detail: Declaring a method that always throws is a runtime substitute for the static guarantee the type system was offering. The precondition 'this format is read-only' belongs in construction or in a separate read-only interface, not deferred to a thrown exception discovered at write time. Defensive-as-substitute for a correctness boundary the compiler could have enforced.

issues.description: Dead constructor parameters retained after numMergeWorkers/mergeExec removal.
issues.detail: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat keeps a constructor accepting numMergeWorkers and ExecutorService, validates them, then discards them. The postcondition of the constructor no longer matches its signature: parameters that have no effect on observable state. Either remove them or document precisely why a read-only format still accepts execution-policy arguments.

issues.description: Protected fields downgraded to package-private while class remains public and extensible.
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues is still an abstract public class, but its members lost the 'protected' qualifier. Subclasses outside the package can no longer access state they previously could. The inheritance contract was changed without stating the new invariant -- either seal the class or restore the access modifier deliberately.

issues.description: Test-only RW format class lives in package with package-private inheritance from production class -- fragile boundary.
issues.detail: Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat reaches into package-private fields (confidenceInterval, bits, compress, flatVectorScorer, rawVectorFormat) of the production class to reconstruct writer behavior. This is correct only because tests share the package. The dependency is undeclared in any type; one accidental rename in production silently breaks tests. State the contract explicitly.

review.summary: The move is mechanical and largely sound, but the discipline of structured boundaries was loosened in three places. First, a magic constant (DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT) is now duplicated across format classes without a stated invariant binding the two definitions. Second, read-only enforcement is delegated to runtime throws rather than expressed in the type system -- a textbook defensive-as-substitute. Third, vestigial constructor parameters (numMergeWorkers, mergeExec) survive on a format that has explicitly disclaimed writing. The work is REASONED enough to land, but only after these boundary lapses are tightened.
